skill.name: frontend-dev-guidelines
skill.description: Frontend development guidelines for React and TypeScript applications using Suspense, TanStack Query, TanStack Router, MUI v7, feature folders, and performance patterns.
skill.summary: Apply consistent React and TypeScript frontend patterns for components, routing, data fetching, styling, and performance.
skill.author: diet103

content.value_statement: React projects often drift across data fetching, routing, styling, and file organization. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code clear frontend patterns to apply.
actual_capabilities: Guides React component structure with TypeScript props and exports.
Shows Suspense and useSuspenseQuery patterns for data fetching.
Explains TanStack Router file routes and lazy route loading.
Defines MUI v7 styling patterns using sx and typed style objects.
Recommends feature folder structure, import aliases, and public exports.
Documents performance patterns such as memoization, debouncing, and cleanup.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a runnable frontend framework.
It assumes React, TypeScript, MUI v7, TanStack Query, and TanStack Router.
It does not validate project dependencies or install packages.
Some examples require adaptation to local API and route names.

use_cases.title: Create a Feature Module
use_cases.description: Use the feature folder pattern to organize API services, hooks, components, helpers, and shared types.

use_cases.title: Standardize Review Guidance
use_cases.description: Check frontend pull requests against consistent rules for loading states, imports, styling, and TypeScript usage.

use_cases.title: Onboard to a React Codebase
use_cases.description: Learn the expected project structure, route patterns, data fetching approach, and common component conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a React TypeScript component for [purpose]. Follow the frontend-dev-guidelines skill for props, loading states, styling, and exports.

prompt_templates.title: Add Data Fetching
prompt_templates.prompt: Add data fetching for [entity]. Use useSuspenseQuery, a feature API service, typed query keys, and the cache-first guidance where useful.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Route Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a new [feature] route using TanStack Router. Include the feature folder structure, lazy loading, Suspense, API service, hooks, and types.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Frontend Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this frontend code for guideline alignment. Refactor loading states, route loading, MUI styling, imports, TypeScript types, and performance issues.

output_examples.input: Create a user profile component that fetches a user by id.
output: A typed React component with a clear props interface.
A Suspense query hook connected to a feature API service.
MUI sx styling and a default export pattern.

output_examples.input: Add a posts route with lazy loading.
output: A TanStack Router route file with a lazy loaded feature component.
A feature folder outline for posts API, hooks, components, and types.
A Suspense boundary recommendation for stable loading behavior.

output_examples.input: Review this dashboard for performance issues.
output: A list of memoization, callback, and list rendering improvements.
Cleanup guidance for effects, timers, listeners, and fetch cancellation.
Notes on heavy components that should be lazy loaded.

best_practices: Use the skill before creating routes, feature modules, or shared components.
Keep examples aligned with the project imports, aliases, and API service names.
Ask for a guideline review after large frontend refactors or new feature work.
anti_patterns: Do not apply these patterns to projects that do not use the listed frontend stack.
Do not copy example route names or API paths without adapting them.
Do not replace local design system rules when the project already defines stronger standards.

faq.question: Does this skill write production code?
faq.answer: It guides code generation and review, but the assistant still writes code in your project context.

faq.question: Which frontend stack does it target?
faq.answer: It targets React, TypeScript, MUI v7, TanStack Query, and TanStack Router.

faq.question: Can it help with loading states?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends Suspense boundaries and discourages early loading returns that shift layout.

faq.question: Does it include data fetching patterns?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers useSuspenseQuery, API service files, cache access, mutations, and query configuration.

faq.question: Can Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it install dependencies?
faq.answer: No. It documents frontend conventions and examples. It does not install packages or run setup commands.
